abstract: [Journal of medical imaging (Bellingham, Wash.)] Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia, characterized by the accumulation of amyloid- β and tau aggregates in the brain. Current diagnostic approaches primarily detect mature plaques, but growing evidence suggests that pre-fibrillar aggregates are present earlier in normal-appearing tissue and may provide a valuable window for intervention. We propose the first proof-of-concept end-to-end deep learning (DL) model to identify AD signatures directly from normal-appearing tissue (i.e., background parenchyma) of raw spectral fluorescence data. To develop and evaluate our DL model, we used one million signals extracted from spectral fluorescence images of brain cortex sections collected from wild-type and 5xFAD mice (a transgenic strain carrying five familial human AD mutations). Our results demonstrate that AD-related signatures can indeed be detected in normal-appearing brain cortex regions. Experiments revealed that model performance depends on input dimensions, training set size, and the preprocessing kernel size. The optimal configuration used 1000 × 32 input, 9000 training samples, and a 3 × 3 kernel, achieving ≥ 95 % accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F 1 -score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Importantly, no mice were misclassified, and saliency analysis indicated that a broad range of spectral fluorescence wavelengths contributed to the model's decisions. These findings highlight the potential of DL-based analysis of spectral fluorescence data to enable earlier detection of AD-related changes, supporting a shift toward a more proactive strategy for biomarker discovery.

abstract: [Breast cancer research and treatment] Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. abstract: [International journal of molecular sciences] How can cellular interactions in solid tumors guide molecular interventions against immune suppression? This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) connects immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) states to testable molecular hypotheses. We distinguish observational artificial intelligence (AI) predictions from molecular intervention hypotheses and examine the experimental evidence required to evaluate them. We reviewed patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, molecular design, simulation, and pharmacology using literature identified through 15 October 2026. Adenosine-receptor antagonist discovery and generative protein-binder design illustrated how computational methods contributed to experimentally tested molecular candidates. Native-state structural studies, stromal delivery, and protein degradation broadened the approaches considered. We organized these findings into a proposed framework encompassing in vivo and patient-derived systems, multi-omics mapping, phenotyping of TME states, actionable AI integration, combination-therapy prioritization, and translational testing (IMPACT). A retrospective analysis of a phase III trial illustrated how the framework connects clinical outcomes to questions about mechanism, patient selection, and exposure. The synthesis clarifies the evidence required to connect molecular binding, target engagement, and exposure to patient benefit. IMPACT provides a structure for relating biological context to molecular design and specifying hypotheses for prospective evaluation.

abstract: [Frontiers in pharmacology] Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas, developed through millennia of clinical practice, represent a rich legacy of approximately 100,000 documented prescriptions (99,584 named formula entries in the second edition of the Dictionary of Traditional Chinese Medicine Formulas), yet on average fewer than ten new TCM products were approved annually by China's NMPA from 2013 to 2024 (77 approvals in total). The experience-based screening paradigm is misaligned with the precision medicine framework demanded by metabolic syndrome (MetS), a multi-target disorder affecting an estimated 1.54 billion adults (95% CrI 1.35-1.76) in 2023. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-encompassing knowledge graphs (KGs), large language models (LLMs), and high-throughput experimentation-has been proposed as a solution, its actual readiness for TCM development remains unclear. This review critically examines KG, LLM, and high-throughput validation technologies enabling precision phytomedicine for MetS, providing a realistic roadmap for AI-driven TCM research and development. The three technology streams exhibit asymmetric readiness. At the stream level, knowledge-graph approaches span Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 3-6, large language model approaches span TRL 1-5, and high-throughput validation platforms span TRL 3-5. LLM development is limited by three TCM-specific hallucination types that lack evaluation benchmarks. KG entity recognition is the most mature component, yet reasoning is hindered by the absence of negative data, missing dose-time dimensions, and unencoded monarch-minister-assistant-envoy hierarchies. High-throughput platforms are technically feasible but remain mismatched to MetS functional endpoints-tumor-derived organoid paradigms show limited direct transferability and would require substantial adaptation. Precision phytomedicine must follow a "foundations before algorithms" sequence: institutionalize negative data, build TCM-Hallu benchmarks, establish functional-endpoint evaluation, and develop AI-assisted regulatory review. Algorithmic advances will remain in an incomplete information space until knowledge infrastructure gaps are closed.
zh_abstract: [Frontiers in pharmacology] 中医（TCM）方剂经数千年临床实践发展而来，留下了约 10 万首有文献记载的处方（《中医方剂大辞典》第二版收录有名称的方剂条目 99,584 条），然而 2013 至 2024 年间，中国国家药品监督管理局（NMPA）平均每年批准的中药新产品不足 10 个（共计 77 个）。这种基于经验的筛选模式，与代谢综合征（MetS）所要求的精准医学框架并不相符；代谢综合征是一种多靶点疾病，2023 年估计影响 15.4 亿成年人（95% CrI 1.35-1.76）。尽管有人提出以人工智能（AI）——包括知识图谱（KG）、大语言模型（LLM）和高通量实验——作为解决方案，但其在中药研发中的实际成熟度仍不明确。本综述对支持代谢综合征精准植物药研究的知识图谱、大语言模型和高通量验证技术进行了批判性审视，为 AI 驱动的中药研发提供一份切合实际的路线图。这三条技术路线的成熟度并不对称。就技术路线整体而言，知识图谱方法处于技术就绪水平（TRL）3-6，大语言模型方法处于 TRL 1-5，高通量验证平台处于 TRL 3-5。大语言模型的发展受限于三种中药特有的幻觉类型，而这些类型缺乏评估基准。知识图谱中的实体识别是最成熟的部分，但推理受到以下因素阻碍：缺乏阴性数据、缺失剂量-时间维度，以及君臣佐使层级关系未被编码。高通量平台在技术上可行，但与代谢综合征的功能性终点仍不匹配——源自肿瘤的类器官范式可直接迁移的程度有限，需要大幅调整。精准植物药必须遵循“先基础、后算法”的顺序：将阴性数据制度化、构建 TCM-Hallu 基准、建立功能性终点评价体系，并发展 AI 辅助的监管审评。在知识基础设施的缺口得到弥补之前，算法的进步仍将处于信息不完整的空间之中。

abstract: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] Deep learning has become an important computational approach in dermatology because it enables automated segmentation and classification of skin lesions. Manual dermoscopic analysis is time-consuming and depends on specialist expertise, with potential inter-observer variability. There is a need to develop reliable computer-aided diagnostic tools. This structured narrative review covers journal papers published mainly from 2018 to 2026 on skin lesion analysis with focus on image preprocessing, benchmark datasets, conventional machine learning approaches, convolutional neural networks, U-Net architectures, transfer learning approaches, Vision Transformers, attention-based models, ensemble solutions, and hybrid segmentation-classification systems. Building on present reviews covering individual tasks as well as broader segmentation-classification pipelines, the present work provides a critical development-to-deployment analysis connecting dataset characteristics, preprocessing, segmentation, classification, evaluation, explainability, robustness, fairness, computational requirements, and clinical applicability. The paper describes widely used evaluation metrics and explains why results obtained across different datasets, partitions, and experimental setups should not be directly compared. Major open problems include class imbalance, data bias, domain shift, limited representation of diverse skin tones, inadequate external validation, computational requirements, and limited explainability of efficient models. Emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, Transformers, foundation models, explainable AI, federated learning, and multi-modal clinical data are reviewed as well. The review offers practical advice to researchers and clinicians on how to approach the preprocessing, segmentation, classification, and evaluation of skin lesions and highlights priorities in developing clinically reliable skin lesion analysis systems.
zh_abstract: [Frontiers in artificial intelligence] 深度学习能够实现皮肤病变的自动分割与分类，已成为皮肤病学中一种重要的计算方法。人工皮肤镜分析耗时，依赖专科医师的专业经验，并可能存在观察者间差异，因此有必要开发可靠的计算机辅助诊断工具。本结构化叙述性综述主要涵盖2018年至2026年发表的皮肤病变分析期刊论文，重点关注图像预处理、基准数据集、传统机器学习方法、卷积神经网络、U-Net架构、迁移学习方法、视觉Transformer（Vision Transformers）、基于注意力的模型、集成方案以及分割-分类混合系统。在现有针对单项任务以及更广泛的分割-分类流程的综述基础上，本文提供了一项从开发到部署的批判性分析，将数据集特征、预处理、分割、分类、评估、可解释性、稳健性、公平性、计算需求和临床适用性联系起来。本文介绍了广泛使用的评估指标，并解释了为何不应直接比较在不同数据集、数据划分和实验设置下获得的结果。主要的未解决问题包括类别不平衡、数据偏倚、领域偏移、不同肤色的代表性有限、外部验证不足、计算需求以及高效模型的可解释性有限。本文还综述了自监督学习、Transformer、基础模型、可解释人工智能、联邦学习和多模态临床数据等新兴趋势。本综述为研究人员和临床医生如何开展皮肤病变的预处理、分割、分类和评估提供了实用建议，并强调了开发临床可靠的皮肤病变分析系统的优先事项。

abstract: 2D-to-3D image registration is a key component for several medical imaging purposes such as intraoperative guidance, enabling the alignment between preoperative 3D volumes and real-time 2D images. While conventional optimisation-based methods often struggle with non-convex objectives, sensitivity to initialisation, and high computational demands, deep learning (DL) has emerged as a promising alternative, offering improved alignment robustness and the potential for real-time performance. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of DL frameworks developed to address the challenges inherent in 2D-to-3D registration. We first outline how core concepts of DL are adapted to the registration problem. We then examine recent methodological advancements from multiple perspectives, including pipeline design, architectural innovations, and domain adaptation strategies. Particular attention is given to quantitative metrics, highlighting how performance is defined and measured across studies. Across the 41 included studies, we find that direct regression is the most common pipeline (23 studies, against 18 iterative ones), that hybrid CNN-attention architectures are gaining ground, and that research remains heavily concentrated on X-ray-to-CT registration. We conclude by identifying the absence of per-case uncertainty estimation and the strong neglect of temporal or sequential modelling as the two methodological gaps most consequential for clinical readiness, and discuss state-space models as a way to add temporal memory within intraoperative latency budgets. Further opportunities lie in more principled domain adaptation and in the integration of foundation models for representation learning.
zh_abstract: 2D 到 3D 图像配准是多种医学影像应用（如术中引导）的关键组成部分，可实现术前 3D 容积与实时 2D 图像之间的对齐。传统基于优化的方法常受困于非凸目标函数、对初始化敏感以及计算需求高，而深度学习（DL）已成为一种有前景的替代方案，可提高配准的稳健性，并具备实时运行的潜力。本综述对为应对 2D 到 3D 配准固有挑战而开发的深度学习框架进行了全面分析。我们首先概述 DL 的核心概念如何适配于配准问题。随后从流程设计、架构创新和领域适应策略等多个角度考察近期的方法学进展。我们特别关注定量指标，着重说明各研究如何定义和衡量性能。在纳入的 41 项研究中，我们发现直接回归是最常见的流程（23 项研究，迭代式流程为 18 项），CNN-注意力混合架构正逐渐增多，且研究仍高度集中于 X 线到 CT 的配准。最后，我们指出，缺乏逐病例的不确定性估计以及严重忽视时间或序列建模，是对临床应用就绪度影响最大的两个方法学缺口，并讨论了状态空间模型作为在术中延迟预算内增加时间记忆的一种途径。进一步的机会在于更有原则的领域适应，以及整合基础模型用于表征学习。

title: A Tumour-Aware Multimodal Framework for Explainable Prediction of IDH Mutation in Gliomas from Multi-Sequence MRI

abstract: Accurate prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status is essential for glioma diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. Although recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated promising performance, many rely on whole-brain feature extraction and provide limited interpretability. This study proposes a tumour-aware multimodal framework for explainable, non-invasive prediction of IDH mutation status from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The proposed framework integrates four MRI sequences (T1, T1CE, T2, and FLAIR), tumour subregion segmentation, quantitative radiomic descriptors, and clinical information within a unified deep learning architecture. An ablation study was conducted to evaluate the contribution of tumour-aware learning, radiomic features, and clinical variables. Model performance was assessed using multiple complementary evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, balanced accuracy, receiver operating characteristic analysis, confusion matrix evaluation, and Grad-CAM visualisation. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed multimodal framework consistently outperformed the baseline MRI-only model, with the Clinical Fusion model achieving the strongest overall predictive performance. The integration of tumour-aware learning, radiomic descriptors, and clinical information progressively improved classification performance, while Grad-CAM visualisations indicated that the model predominantly focused on biologically relevant tumour regions. These findings suggest that tumour-aware multimodal feature integration enables accurate, interpretable, and non-invasive molecular profiling of gliomas and provides a promising foundation for future clinical decision support in precision neuro-oncology.

abstract: Precise classification of laryngeal lesions is clinically crucial yet highly challenging, as inter-class visual differences are often subtle. While abnormalities in vocal fold vibratory dynamics provide complementary discriminative information, existing deep learning models predominantly rely on visual appearance and lack explicit mechanisms for modeling clinically meaningful vibratory dynamics. To address this, we propose PADSNet, a Physics-Aware Dual-Stream Network for laryngeal lesion classification that integrates visual representations with explicit biomechanical reasoning. Specifically, a Wavelet-Attention Enhancement Module (WAEM) is designed to bridge the spectral-semantic gap, enabling complementary learning of spatial texture and dynamic frequency representations. Meanwhile, a Knowledge Computing Module (KCM) extracts interpretable biomechanical indices from temporal glottal distance waveforms, including indicators of mobility, symmetry, glottal closure, and vibration stability. These descriptors are subsequently incorporated into a Physics-Aware Gating Module (PAGM) as biomechanical priors to adaptively recalibrate visual feature toward pathology-relevant vibratory patterns. Extensive experiments on a clinical dataset demonstrate that PADSNet achieves an accuracy of 0.8452, an F1-score of 0.8090, a sensitivity of 0.7953, and a specificity of 0.8866. These results indicate that explicitly integrating biomechanical priors with deep visual representations provides a more accurate, robust, and clinically interpretable framework for automated laryngeal lesion classification.

abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Introduction: Nurse-led telephone triage, frequently guided by the United Kingdom Oncology Nursing Society (UKONS) tool, is a cornerstone of supportive oncology care, yet the appropriateness of triage decisions varies across settings. Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in medical communication but remain unvalidated for autonomous clinical decision-making, particularly in gynecologic oncology, where remote and telephone-based care pose distinct challenges. Methods and Materials: Twenty fictitious case vignettes representing common treatment-related toxicities in gynecologic oncology were developed. Three board-certified gynecologic consultants independently assigned UKONS Red-Amber-Green (RAG) triage categories, reaching unanimous consensus that served as the reference standard. Vignettes were submitted verbatim, as single-turn queries with no follow-up prompting, to three publicly available LLMs (OpenEvidence, ChatGPT, Google Gemini). LLM responses were mapped to RAG categories and compared descriptively against the reference standard, stratified by treatment type and platform. Results: All three LLMs achieved 100% concordance with the reference standard for all Red cases across both treatment groups, with no high-acuity case downgraded to self-care. Discrepancies clustered at lower-acuity boundaries. In the chemotherapy-alone group, errors were limited to omission of an explicit 24-h follow-up window for 1 Amber-rated complaints. In the combined group, all LLMs over-triaged intermediate-risk complaints toward immediate or same-day evaluation; low-risk complaints showed more variable over-triage. Conclusions: LLMs identified unambiguous emergent gynecologic oncology symptoms, preserving the UKONS safety floor, but showed relatively reduced precision and a conservative over-triage bias at lower-acuity margins, especially in the combined-therapy collective. These findings support a supervised, adjunctive role for LLMs, rather than autonomous deployment, pending prospective validation.

【方法与材料】编制了20个虚构病例情景，代表妇科肿瘤中常见的治疗相关毒性。三位具有董事会认证资质的妇科顾问医师独立给出UKONS红-琥珀-绿（RAG）分诊类别，并达成一致意见，作为参考标准。这些情景以原文形式、作为单轮查询（无后续提示）提交给三种公开可用的LLM（OpenEvidence、ChatGPT、Google Gemini）。将LLM的回复映射到RAG类别，并按治疗类型和平台分层，与参考标准进行描述性比较。

abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] Background/Objectives: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) and periodontitis are two of the most common chronic conditions sharing an underlying mechanism represented by systemic inflammation. Smart technologies, including machine learning (ML), wearable and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, telemedicine and intraoral sensors, are increasingly used in both fields. This narrative review examined how these technologies are used to predict, monitor and manage MetS and oral diseases and what evidence supports combining oral and metabolic data. Methods: Following the SANRA framework, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English-language articles published between January 2021 and May 2026. Of the 6922 records identified (3520 after de-duplication), 1852 were screened by title and abstract, and studies were selected by relevance to three research questions. Applications were classified by their current level of evidence. Results: ML models for MetS prediction often reported high discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] up to 0.99), but most were validated only internally, and several used the diagnostic components of MetS as predictors. Wearable, telemedicine and mobile interventions, usually combined with lifestyle programs, were associated with improvements in body weight, blood pressure and glycemic markers; artificial intelligence tools for dental imaging showed accuracy comparable to clinicians in mostly retrospective studies, with limited evidence on patient outcomes. Few studies combined oral and metabolic data: cross-sectional ML studies identified periodontal severity as a predictor of MetS and metabolic conditions as predictors of periodontitis, and salivary glucose correlated with blood glucose mainly in people living with diabetes, which does not establish diagnostic accuracy. No prospective study has tested an integrated dental-medical pathway. Conclusions: Integrating oral and metabolic data through smart technologies is biologically plausible and appears technically feasible, but its added diagnostic value, clinical effectiveness and cost effectiveness have not been established. Externally validated models, prospective cohorts and trials of integrated care pathways are required before routine use.
zh_abstract: 【背景/目的】代谢综合征（MetS）和牙周炎是两种最常见的慢性疾病，二者具有以全身炎症为代表的共同潜在机制。包括机器学习（ML）、可穿戴设备和物联网（IoT）设备、远程医疗以及口内传感器在内的智能技术，正越来越多地应用于这两个领域。本叙述性综述探讨了这些技术如何用于预测、监测和管理 MetS 及口腔疾病，以及有哪些证据支持将口腔数据与代谢数据相结合。【方法】按照 SANRA 框架，检索 PubMed、Scopus 和 Web of Science 中 2021 年 1 月至 2026 年 5 月发表的英文文献。共检出 6922 条记录（去重后 3520 条），其中 1852 条经标题和摘要筛选，并根据与三个研究问题的相关性选择研究。应用按其当前证据水平进行分类。【结果】用于 MetS 预测的 ML 模型常报告较高的区分度（受试者操作特征曲线下面积 [AUC] 最高达 0.99），但大多数仅经内部验证，且有若干模型将 MetS 的诊断组分用作预测变量。可穿戴设备、远程医疗和移动干预（通常与生活方式项目联合应用）与体重、血压和血糖指标的改善相关；用于牙科影像的人工智能工具在以回顾性为主的研究中显示出与临床医生相当的准确性，但关于患者结局的证据有限。结合口腔与代谢数据的研究很少：横断面 ML 研究发现牙周病严重程度可预测 MetS，代谢状况可预测牙周炎；唾液葡萄糖主要在糖尿病患者中与血糖相关，但这并不能确立其诊断准确性。尚无前瞻性研究检验过整合的牙科—内科路径。【结论】通过智能技术整合口腔和代谢数据在生物学上合理，在技术上似乎可行，但其附加诊断价值、临床有效性和成本效益尚未确立。在常规使用之前，需要经外部验证的模型、前瞻性队列研究以及整合照护路径的试验。

abstract: [Frontiers in oral health] Orthodontic extraction decision-making requires integration of multiple diagnostic characteristics, yet the factors underlying extraction vs. non-extraction treatment selection have not been comprehensively synthesized across conventional clinical research and contemporary prediction models. This systematic review aimed to identify and critically evaluate the diagnostic factors influencing orthodontic extraction decisions and determine their consistency across the available evidence. PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through July 2026 for studies evaluating diagnostic factors associated with orthodontic extraction decisions or statistical or artificial intelligence-based prediction models. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis, and findings were synthesized narratively. Nineteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Dental crowding and tooth size -arch length discrepancy were the most consistently evaluated diagnostic factors but were typically considered alongside facial profile, incisor position, skeletal relationships, and occlusal characteristics. No consistent numerical threshold for recommending extraction was identified. Artificial intelligence-based prediction models demonstrated promising performance, with interpretable predictors substantially overlapping with diagnostic variables identified in conventional clinical studies. Methodological quality ranged from moderate to critical risk of bias, with most prediction-model studies judged to be at high risk of bias. These findings indicate that orthodontic extraction decision-making is fundamentally multifactorial rather than governed by a single diagnostic measurement or threshold. Current artificial intelligence models should be considered decision-support tools pending higher-quality prospective research and external validation; whether image-derived or latent features provide genuinely novel determinants of extraction need remains uncertain. https://osf.io/x86zy.

abstract: Conductors are critical for the performance of an orchestra even though they do not emit sound. Basic research and clinical studies in the last decade are revealing that astrocytes may be the "conductors" of the "orchestra" that is the brain network: astrocytes make up approximately $50\%$ of all brain cells but do not emit electrical signals. Nevertheless, they may play critical roles in important cognitive brain functions, specifically learning, memory, and information processing. Here we consider the implications of these discoveries for brain-inspired machine learning (ML), where analogy is typically drawn between neurons and their electrical interactions. We highlight specific algorithms for two key astrocyte characteristics. The first characteristic is the ability to link to and modulate thousands of synapses simultaneously. A model based on this characteristic yields faster training and makes the network more robust to noise, providing a supervised learning algorithm that can be applied to any existing neural network. The second characteristic we focus on is that the non-electrical communication among astrocytes includes slow, rhythmic dynamics. The rhythmic sharing algorithm we developed based on this premise yields rapid anomaly detection adaptation and prevents catastrophic forgetting. Overall, we find that astrocyte-derived algorithms outperform neurocentric algorithms significantly and remediate critical weaknesses of current state-of-the-art ML models.
